security_audit.summary: Most Markdown backtick findings are documentation examples, but the skill repeatedly recommends curl-to-shell installation and manifest-driven shell commands. It also enables cloud file uploads and Twitter/X automation, which require explicit consent and careful credential controls. No prompt injection text was found.

remediation.suggestion: Replace curl-to-shell examples with download, verify, inspect, then execute steps. Pin checksums or signatures in the documentation.
Avoid shell command substitution for remote manifests. Provide explicit platform URLs or a verified installer with detached signature checks.
Warn users before uploading local files. Require explicit paths and avoid suggesting parent-directory paths for sensitive data.
Require explicit user confirmation before any post, DM, follow, like, or retweet action.
Add guidance for scoped API keys, secret storage, and key rotation after accidental exposure.

content.user_title: Run Inference.sh AI Apps from Your Agent
content.value_statement: AI agents often need many hosted models without custom API wiring. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through inference.sh CLI discovery, authentication, and app execution.
actual_capabilities: Shows how to install and authenticate the inference.sh CLI.
Lists commands for discovering apps by category, search term, featured status, and pagination.
Provides examples for running image, video, LLM, search, 3D, audio, and Twitter/X apps.
Explains local file inputs for image, audio, video, and media upload workflows.
Documents task tracking, asynchronous runs, result retrieval, and output saving.
Links to reference files for setup, app discovery, running apps, and CLI commands.
limitations: Requires the inference.sh CLI and an authenticated account before app runs can succeed.
Depends on external cloud services, model availability, quotas, and account permissions.
Local file paths may upload files to cloud services when used as app inputs.
Twitter/X actions require valid credentials and explicit user approval before publishing.

use_cases.title: Prototype AI media workflows
use_cases.description: Run image, video, audio, and 3D generation apps from one CLI workflow.

use_cases.title: Explore hosted model options
use_cases.description: Search app catalogs, inspect schemas, generate sample inputs, and compare available cloud models.

use_cases.title: Automate agent tasks with hosted apps
use_cases.description: Submit long-running jobs, check task status, retrieve outputs, and save results for later use.

prompt_templates.title: List available apps
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to list inference.sh apps for image generation. Show the most relevant options and note any account requirements.

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an app run
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to inspect the input requirements for a video generation app and create a safe run plan.

prompt_templates.title: Run and monitor a task
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to run a long video task without waiting, then show how to check status and retrieve the result.

prompt_templates.title: Design a multi-app workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Use agent-tools to combine search, LLM analysis, and media generation apps into a reviewed workflow with approval points.

output_examples.input: Ask for available image generation apps related to FLUX.
output_examples.output: A short list of matching inference.sh apps, their categories, and the next command to inspect input requirements.

output_examples.input: Run a video generation app as a background task.
output_examples.output: A task identifier, the command to check status later, and a reminder that cloud processing may take time.

output_examples.input: Prepare a local image upscaling workflow.
output_examples.output: A plan that confirms the file path, explains upload behavior, and asks before sending the file to the service.

best_practices: Inspect app schemas before each run so inputs match the selected app.
Ask for explicit approval before uploading local files or publishing social media actions.
Use scoped API keys and avoid storing credentials in shared project files.
anti_patterns: Do not pipe remote installer scripts directly into a shell without inspection.
Do not pass broad directory paths or sensitive files as app inputs.
Do not automate posts, DMs, follows, likes, or retweets without user confirmation.

faq.question: What does this skill help an agent do?
faq.answer: It helps an agent use the inference.sh CLI to discover apps, run hosted models, and track task results.

faq.question: Does it require an inference.sh account?
faq.answer: Yes. Authentication is required for most app runs, task tracking, and account-specific commands.

faq.question: Can it run image and video generation?
faq.answer: Yes. The references include image, video, audio, 3D, LLM, search, and utility app examples.

faq.question: Can it upload local files?
faq.answer: Yes. The CLI can upload local file paths when an app input accepts a file or URL.

faq.question: Can it publish to Twitter or X?
faq.answer: The examples include Twitter/X actions. The agent should request explicit approval before any public or account action.

faq.question: Is installation risk-free?
faq.answer: No. The current documentation includes pipe-to-shell installation examples that should be replaced with verified steps.
